checks.label: Add a nonzero multiple of one row to another row: on the row-move screen every pick of two different rows and a nonzero multiplier changes that one row, swings its plane about the line it shares with the added row's plane, and leaves the dot where it was

The equations are replaced by a system having the same solution but in triangular form, then solved by back-substitution: the staircase screen ends with zeros under the diagonal and the first grid's answer, and its lines find z, then y, then x

A system may have a unique solution, an infinity of solutions or no solution at all: the first planes meet at one dot; the grid whose bottom row ends as zero equals a number other than zero has no dot and three side-by-side lines; the grid whose bottom row is all zeros has a shared line, every point of which fits

Breaking the circuit into simple loops leads to a set of linear equations in the unknown currents: each loop's row holds its total resistance on the diagonal and minus each shared resistance beside it, and the currents found fit every first row

Every worked number is right: −2 × row 1 makes row 2 [0 −1 −3 | −11]; −1 × row 1 makes row 3 [0 −2 1 | −1] (5 and 11 are the slips); −2 × row 2 makes [0 0 7 | 21], so z = 3, y = 2 and x = 1, and (1, 2, 3) gives 6, 1 and 5; the staircase puzzle gives (2, 1, 2), with 0 and 1 the slips; the grid ending 9 steps to 0 = 5 and the one ending 4 to 0 = 0, both with determinant 0; the line is (2 − t, 1, t); the third grid steps to [0 −3 3 | −3] and 0 = 0; the circuit's determinant is 324, row 2 becomes [0 21 −6 | 12] and row 3 [0 0 36 | 54], giving 1.5 A, 1 A and 2.5 A, with −7.5 + 12 − 4.5 = 0 and 0.5 A against loop 2 (18 and 6 are the slips); the last grid ends 0 = 1
Each puzzle's answer comes from the rule, and each wrong answer offered is the slip its hint names
Each puzzle offers three different answers, accepts only the right one, and draws every wrong one in the warning colour
Before Check, no puzzle shows its answer; after a right answer, it does
On the line screen, at every t the slider can take, the dot sits at (2 − t, 1, t) on the shared line, and putting it into each first equation gives back that equation's constant

Each demonstration ends where the lesson says: the first planes meet at (1, 2, 3); row 2 becomes [0 −1 −3 | −11] with the dot unmoved; the grid ending 9 has no dot; the circuit's row 2 becomes [0 21 −6 | 12]
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 3 to 5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 3 s
